_what: THE FSHARP NAME CEILING IS SHAPE-DEPENDENT — THE FIX IS NOT BUILT, and this is condition 5 firing rather than a refusal to work.
_instrument: .tmp-fsharp-gateshape.mts (the GATE'S OWN SHAPE: a global stride of 150 of 11,807 files, key space built from those files) against fsharp-name-ceiling.mts (a DIFFERENT shape: 30 files per repo in 8 repos, per-repo key space)

threeMeasurementsOfTheSameQuestion.predicate: filename-STEM proxy, no key space at all
THE GATE'S OWN SHAPE — global stride 150, key space 8,494 names

theReading: THE READINGS RANGE FROM 7.6% TO 28.6% FOR THE SAME QUESTION, and the variable is the SHAPE, not the corpus: the gate's global stride leaves ~6 files per repository, so a project publishes few names and few targets can resolve; a per-repo sample of 30 files leaves five times more. **Neither is the population.** The 40.4% ceiling I reported is a per-repo-sample number and does NOT hold on the gate's own shape — which is why the fix is not built on it.

whatWouldSettleIt.theRun: the WHOLE-POPULATION fsharp row (`incoming-gate.ts fsharp fs,fsi,fsx 0`), ~11,807 files, ~40 minutes — the same population as the before-arm it must be paired with
whatWouldSettleIt.whyNotRunHere: the machine is at 0-1 GB available with load 24 and seven lanes working; a 40-minute run risks being KILLED at its bound, and TWO of this lane's runs already were. The Lead offered to hold the lease for long runs, and this is one.
whatWouldSettleIt.theDecisionItFeeds: if the population ceiling is a few hundred edges or more, the fix is worth building and the shape is already named (emit the spelling the project publishes, or do not fire); if it is tens, the lane's residual is a BOUNDARY like r's packages and the cause closes as ruled.

THE_R_RULING.ruled: r's imports residue is a PACKAGE cause and it is a BOUNDARY, not a gap
THE_R_RULING.mechanism: `library()`/`require()` name CRAN packages; packages are not in the corpus, so there is no declaration to reach and a file claim reaches 3 edges (+24 `.cpp` refutes that must NOT be admitted: files on disk, extensions this lane cannot hold)
THE_R_RULING.falsifier: a corpus that CONTAINS those packages moves the count; until then the file route must not be widened to reach them, and the 24 refutes are the evidence

EARNED: The ceiling question was measured FOUR ways, with three predicates agreeing in a 20.7-28.6% band on a per-repo shape and a fourth giving 7.6% on the gate's shape — and the disagreement is the finding, not a nuisance.
The shape-dependence was caught BEFORE a fix was built on it: the sample ceiling (40.4%) does not hold on the gate's own shape, so condition 5 applies and the build stops here.

The instrument error that produced the widest reading was identified: my union key space over an 8,494-name set counts a target published in repo A as resolvable for an edge in repo B, while the gate resolves PER PROJECT.
r is RULED as a boundary with its count, mechanism and falsifier — a complete result on a lane nobody owns.
NOT_EARNED: THE FIX IS NOT BUILT and NO before/after exists: `unresolved` vs `noDecl` separated, `bindFAIL` 0, and the 11 `_lib/Fornax.Core.dll` refutes still unadmitted are all UNMEASURED for this change.
THE POPULATION CEILING IS UNMEASURED on fsharp (and on the other HIGH-ceiling lanes) — the 40.4% and the 7.6% are both samples and neither is a lane's number.
No store run for any of this lane's work.

IT_IS_THE_GATES_OWN_DOCUMENTED_LIMITATIO.theNote: "a stride sample cannot measure a FILE-SCOPED target: an import that names a path in the same project resolves only if that project's other files are in the key space, so a sampled run understates import resolution by construction (measured: 0.4 % sampled vs 46.8 % whole-corpus on the same revision). A whole single project is the honest unit for any question about file-scoped targets."
IT_IS_THE_GATES_OWN_DOCUMENTED_LIMITATIO.andItsRule: "THE UNSAMPLED ADMITTED POPULATION — `files` before the stride. A project fact (is this path in the population at all?) must be answered from THIS, not from the sample, or a claim would be verified against the run's budget instead of against the project."
IT_IS_THE_GATES_OWN_DOCUMENTED_LIMITATIO.whatThatMakesOfTheFourWaySpread: NOT a new defect: it is the documented limitation measured on this lane, with numbers the note did not have. The 7.6% is a statement about THE SHAPE, and now also about the gate, not about fsharp's fixability.
IT_IS_THE_GATES_OWN_DOCUMENTED_LIMITATIO.theFleetConsequence: ANY lane that quoted a stride reading for a file-scoped target understated it by construction — the note's own pair is 0.4% sampled against 46.8% whole-corpus, a factor of 117. Several lanes have stride rows; this is the first to price the gap.

WHICH_OF_THIS_LANES_NUMBERS_THE_STRIDE_D.NOT_AFFECTED: Every FILE CLAIM figure — protobuf's 304 then 993 of 1,061, scss 3,108, clean 429, lua's ceiling — because each was resolved against the UNSAMPLED admitted list (`git ls-files` per lane, then only the PARSING was sampled), which is the rule the gate states at the `admitted` field. Verified by reading the probes: the admitted set is built from all tracked files before any stride is applied.
WHICH_OF_THIS_LANES_NUMBERS_THE_STRIDE_D.AFFECTED: Every KEY-SPACE figure — the 7.6% stride ceiling, and the gate's own `resolved`/`unresolved` columns on any stride run. That is why the population row and the stride row must be recorded SIDE BY SIDE: a reader with only the population number does not know a 150-file stride reads 7.6% on this lane, and a reader with only 7.6% would conclude the cause is unfixable when it may be entirely fixable.
